about: ORCA geofence layers. Every feature states its authority and accuracy. Only features with accuracy 'official' may be treated as legal boundaries; all others are for demonstration and MUST be replaced with authoritative layers (NHO charts, MoES/INCOIS, MoEFCC/WDPA) before operational use.

features.name: India–Sri Lanka maritime boundary (Palk Strait & Gulf of Mannar)
features.authority: India–Sri Lanka maritime boundary agreements (1974 Palk Strait, 1976 Gulf of Mannar)
features.reference: Agreement between India and Sri Lanka on the Boundary in Historic Waters (1974), Art. 1; Agreement on the Maritime Boundary in the Gulf of Mannar and the Bay of Bengal (1976), Art. 1 — texts: UN DOALOS Delimitation Treaties Infobase (LKA-IND1974BW.PDF, LKA-IND1976MB.PDF)
features.accuracy_note: All turning points checked against the treaty texts: 1974 positions 1–6 and 1976 positions 1m–13m (1976 position 4m reads '79° 18'.2 N' in the text, taken as E). Treaty great-circle arcs are drawn as straight lines between points (differences of metres at these lengths). Charts (NHO) remain the legal reference at sea.
features.rule: Crossing the international maritime boundary without authorization is prohibited.

features.name: India–Sri Lanka maritime boundary (Bay of Bengal)
features.authority: Agreement between India and Sri Lanka on the Maritime Boundary in the Gulf of Mannar and the Bay of Bengal (1976)
features.reference: 1976 Agreement, Art. 2 (positions 1b, 1ba, 1bb, 2b–6b) — text: UN DOALOS Delimitation Treaties Infobase (LKA-IND1976MB.PDF)
features.accuracy_note: Turning points checked against the treaty text. The agreement leaves the extension beyond position 6b to be settled later; ORCA draws only the agreed part.
features.rule: Crossing the international maritime boundary without authorization is prohibited.

features.name: India–Bangladesh maritime boundary (Bay of Bengal)
features.authority: Bay of Bengal Maritime Boundary Arbitration (Bangladesh v. India), Award of 7 July 2014 (PCA / UNCLOS Annex VII)
features.reference: Award, Technical Report paras 16, 23–24: Delimitation Points 1–3 (WGS-84), then a geodetic line at azimuth 177° 30' 00" to its intersection with the Bangladesh/Myanmar line at 16° 43' 28.77" N, 89° 25' 54.39" E — RIAA vol. XXXII pp. 1–182 (legal.un.org)
features.accuracy_note: Points from the Award; the long southern leg is a geodesic drawn here as a straight line (a few hundred metres at most at 490 km). Charts (NHO) remain the legal reference at sea.
features.rule: Crossing the international maritime boundary without authorization is prohibited.
